title: Eurostat euro-area HICP flash estimate (September 2026) — publishes 2026-10-02, the morning US payrolls may not
source: EST: THE DATE IS CORRECTED IN THIS FILE — the release is 2026-10-02, NOT the 2026-10-01 the id slug says. The slug is the proposal's DERIVED guess and is kept only as this event's stable key: scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs keys a file name to its id and never to its date, and renaming the id would strand the ledger, the forward-test fragment and the research branch that all key off it. Two primaries fetched direct 2026-09-09 agree on 10-02. (1) Eurostat's own August flash release, ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-01092026-ap, carries the line 'Next release: 2 October 2026' — the SAME field that on the June flash (2-01072026-ap) read 'Next release: 31 July 2026' and correctly named the July flash, so the convention is tested and not assumed. (2) The ECB statistical release calendar, ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/statscal/ges/html/sthicp.en.html, lists '02/10/2026 15:00 CET — Euro area seasonally adjusted HICP flash estimate (Dataset: HICP) Reference period: Sep-2026', with the September complete release at '16/10/2026 12:00 CET' and the October flash at '04/11/2026 15:00 CET'. That same calendar's '17/09/2026 12:00 CET' row for the August complete matches Eurostat's own '17 September 2026' sentence, which is how its dates were checked against Eurostat's before being relied on. THE PROPOSAL'S PATTERN IS REFUTED, NOT REFINED: the two-of-three last-working-day reading of 2026-07-01 / 2026-07-31 / 2026-09-01 predicted 10-01 with 09-30 as the alternative, and the true answer (10-02) is neither — Eurostat's flash is SCHEDULED, not derivable from month-end arithmetic. Stays estimate on two counts, either sufficient: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:) has no slot for a non-US statistical agency — the same reason the siblings eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17 and ecb-decision-2026-09-10 are filed estimate despite direct primaries. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, over the single proposal proposals/eurostat-hicp-flash-2026-10-01.from-cpi-2026-09-11.json, which was read first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md and is now inert (shadowed, left in place). FIRST THING TO KNOW: the id says 10-01 and the release is 10-02; see `source`. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS SIBLING, which is the whole reason it earns a slot: eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17 is a RECEIPT — it confirms a number published sixteen days earlier and lands after both policy meetings it could inform. This flash is the opposite: it publishes FIRST, and it lands INSIDE the window that informs the ECB's 2026-10-29 decision, twenty days before the 2026-10-21 quiet period begins. Together with the September complete release (10-16) it is one of only two euro-area inflation reads the Governing Council gets between the 09-10 decision and the 10-29 one. THE ADJACENCY THAT MATTERS MOST IS AMERICAN, NOT EUROPEAN: 10-02 is also Employment Situation day (jobs-2026-10-02, confirmed, high), and it is day two of a possible federal funding lapse (government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 — 'an un-averted lapse removes the 10-02 payrolls'). BLS does not publish through a lapse; Eurostat is not a US agency and does. So in the shutdown branch this low-impact entry becomes one of the few hard macro reads that morning — which is a CALENDAR-VISIBILITY property, never a substitute: euro-area consumer prices say nothing about US labour, and the only honest read-across is to the ENERGY SHOCK both tapes share. THE SHAPE TO WATCH, not the level: August's flash accelerated to 3.3% almost entirely on ENERGY (14.3% y/y, from 10.3%) while SERVICES DECELERATED (3.3% -> 3.0%) and core came in at 2.4%, below a 2.5% consensus — the energy-hot / core-tame shape the cpi-2026-09-11 and ecb-decision-2026-09-10 ledgers both lean on. September's base is unusually soft in two cells (Eurostat's own database, fetched 2026-09-09: September 2025 m/m was energy -0.1%, services -0.9%), so energy y/y rises mechanically on any positive month while services y/y rises unless the package-holiday roll-off repeats. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately and unchanged from the proposal: no house playbook is rates- or euro-keyed, no tracked name carries euro-inflation exposure, and a flash estimate has no US price channel. READ-ACROSS LIMIT, stated so it is not overread later: euro HICP is NOT US core CPI — no owners'-equivalent-rent, where US core's heaviest weight sits, and a higher energy weight (~9.1%), so any comparison is DIRECTIONAL AND NEVER QUANTITATIVE. Filed estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
